name: Stephen Phillips
bio: Stephen Phillips (1868–1915) was an English poet and verse dramatist. He won sudden fame with his Poems of 1897 and with the plays Paolo and Francesca (1899), Herod (1900) and Ulysses (1902), which revived blank-verse drama on the London stage.
His popularity faded within a few years, and he died in 1915. The two short lyrics here come from Untermeyer's Modern British Poetry (1920); the extract from Herod printed there is not included.

poems.title: Beautiful Lie the Dead
poems.author: Stephen Phillips

poems.title: A Dream
poems.author: Stephen Phillips
poems.text:
My dead love came to me, and said:
  'God gives me one hour's rest,
To spend with thee on earth again:
  How shall we spend it best?'

'Why, as of old,' I said; and so
  We quarrelled, as of old:
But, when I turned to make my peace,
  That one short hour was told.
